column1: # The Last Campfire: Hello Games, Unity 2018.4.24f1 IL2CPP, SDK 10.4.1, NVN; update 1.0.5 (v327680).
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) on Linux and checked on an iPhone 16 Pro: 60 fps (frame time p50 16.66 ms, p95 17.1 ms), a 1650 MiB footprint

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie). Everything is in Data/data.unity3d (a UnityFS bundle with no type trees) and Data/Resources

# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory): the 5 GB guest layout with a large alias region. This sdk build is Advance Wars 1+2's and Little Nightmares II's, whose address-region node
# area cut (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) Unity's own reservations need here too
# Engage's reported pool in the same 5 GB layout (the heap check, which needs a Mac, did not run): nninitStartup hands pool − used to StandardAllocator as one address region, and Unity
# reserves its own regions beside it; the guessed 3.2 GB pool would leave those about 1.1 GB of alias region
# Unity 2018.4: 11,435 shaders, the GLSLC outputs of its Shader objects and its 4 ComputeShader objects (unityfs.py COMPUTE_2018_4: Internal-Skinning and the game's FogTextureGenerator,
# whose fog was drawn as flat planes without them). Pre-2019.3 subprograms hold one stage each, so the split pairs no vertex and pixel shader by variant; 2 pipelines whose pixel shader
# reads an output its vertex shader does not write fail to link (a red line each), with nothing seen missing in play
